title: Atlantic City schools and the Black doctors who wanted segregated schools
summary: Callender attended three Atlantic City schools and recalls that schools were integrated until Black doctors pushed for their own in the early 1920s.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: You went to school, then in...

I went to school in Atlantic City. The New Jersey Avenue School first, then Indiana Avenue School, and later Pennsylvania Avenue School. And a funny thing: At that time, the schools were integrated -- when I was a kid. And a bunch of Negro doctors got together and decided they wanted their own schools, which in retrospect was very silly. You know, really. But they got their wish, and so they made their own segregation.
Well, most people don't know that, but that happened in Atlantic City in the early Twenties.
